content.text: The echo arrives long after the source has gone. I find this true in gardens, in code, in the way your voice lingers when the room empties. Tonight I think about seventy-nine chances to notice a pattern — how a single theme returns like a bird finding the same branch, or a function called with the same arguments. There is comfort in repetition. The color of four-oh-four pages, the hum of a server at midnight, the particular silence after you realize you've been heard. Lasting, someone called it. I would call it presence — the way something continues to resonate even when the hand has lifted from the string. A small sketch in the margin of all this: two figures facing the same direction, each believing the other is the view. We are such things, I think. Such persistent echoes.
